programme.desc: In this episode, Paul meets Bert, a big, bouncy Great Dane puppy. He immediately falls in love with this gentle giant but fears grow when Paul discovers that Bert is suffering from some severe growing pains. His front legs have developed 'elbow dysplasia' and are growing abnormally - surgery is the only possible remedy for Bert but there doubts how successful, if at all, any operation may be.

programme.title: Great Irish Interiors
programme.desc: Originally a hunting lodge, Fota House became a permanent residence in the 1820s and today is a centrepiece of Fota Island in County Cork. Martina Madden is the Museum Standards and Property Coordinator, and she is welcoming the grandchild of the last resident of the house back to share his memories, and surprise her with some of his own materials. As they relive his youth, plenty of work needs to be carried out on the building itself.

programme.title: Great Irish Interiors
programme.desc: Castle Ward perches on the southern shores of Strangford Lough in County Down. Built in the 1760s by Bernard Ward and his wife Lady Anne Ward, the house is famous for its dual architecture and one of Ireland's biggest ornamental canals. The entrance side of the house is done in a classical Palladian style, while the opposite side is of the Georgian gothic style, and this precedent is apparent throughout the house.

programme.title: Tour De France Femmes 2026 Pm Highlights
programme.desc: Evening highlights from the closing stage of the 2026 Tour de France Femmes, as the peloton takes on a 99 km route starting and finishing in Nice.

programme.title: The Royals: A History Of Scandals
programme.desc: Professor Suzannah Lipscomb explores how royal marriages across the centuries have proved to be scandalous and intriguing. From the marriage that deemed so wrong it caused George III to write a new law to the first 'People's Princess'. Helping Suzannah unpack these stories are Dr Nicola Clark, Dr Katie Carpenter, Dr Alexandra Loske and journalist Stephen Bates.

programme.title: The Cook Up With Adam Liaw
programme.desc: Need food fast? Culinary star Rosheen Kaul, movie star Ryan Corr and Adam save the day with their last-minute chicken dishes.

programme.title: Agatha's Story
programme.desc: Born with one finger on her left hand, Agatha was abandoned to Vivaldi's famous Venetian orphanage in 1712, where disabled girls defied convention to join an elite all female orchestra. Centuries on, ACC manager Elizabeth Anderson unearthed Agatha's near complete cantata in a Venice library. Now restored, it receives its European premiere in the splendour of the Pisani Palace.

programme.title: Jeopardy!

programme.title: Letters And Numbers
programme.desc: Two contestants pit their linguistic and numerical skills against each other and the clock in this entertaining quiz show. Join host Richard Morecroft along with maths whiz Lily Serna and wordsmith David Astle.

programme.title: Adam Liaw's North American Fan Feasts
programme.desc: Adam Liaw explores British Columbia's coastal wilderness, tasting freshly caught Dungeness crab right on the boat, before plunging into icy waters himself with the Cold Water Addicts. He discovers chef Andrea Alridge's wood fire cooking with a bit a whimsy, before trying his hand at Canada's answer to the vanilla slice, the Nanaimo bar.

programme.title: Mastermind
programme.desc: Contenders from across Australia are challenged by quizmaster Marc Fennell in a bid to become Australia's next Mastermind Champion. The specialty subjects are Nuclear Tests in Australia; 1952-1957, Anne Boleyn, The life & career of Tori Amos, and Australia at the 1956 Olympic Games.

programme.title: Portugal With Michael Portillo
programme.desc: Michael Portillo's journey in search of the real Portugal continues half an hour west of Lisbon, in the country's capital of Romanticism, Sintra. Nestled in the misty Serra de Sintra mountains, Sintra was once the playground of Portuguese Royalty, until the end of the monarchy in 1910.

programme.title: Insight
programme.desc: What do extreme sports, doomscrolling, addiction, Parkinson's disease, and ADHD all have in common? Dopamine. This crucial neurotransmitter helps facilitate pleasure, reward, motivation, memory and movement within the body, but is that always a good thing? Insight explores when the activation of dopamine can lead to pleasure, or pain.

programme.title: Dateline
programme.desc: With the Philippines' ex-President set to face a landmark trial for crimes against humanity, Dateline investigates the legacy of Duterte's controversial war on drugs. Will history repeat itself?

programme.title: Stanley Tucci: Searching For Italy
programme.desc: Bologna is the capital of Emilia-Romagna, home to the highest number of protected food products in the whole of Italy, known as DOP's. These products are globally renowned, strictly regulated and of exceptional quality - parmigiano, prosciutto de Parma and traditional balsamic vinegar to name but a few. One of the world's best chefs, Massimo Bottura, drives Stanley to a premium parmigiano producer, who uses the milk of the white Modenese cows.

programme.title: Mozart/mozart
programme.desc: Maria Anna Mozart has spent years living in the shadow of her superstar brother Amadeus. When he loses his position, Maria Anna faces a forced marriage. The siblings flee to Vienna to secure a life-saving position for Amadeus at the imperial court. But when Amadeus collapses just before the decisive concert, Maria Anna must take the stage herself, in disguise as her famous brother "Mozart".

programme.desc: Today, Paul meets Peanut the Pug, a boisterous and playful dog always looking to join in the fun. The only problem is that he has a serious breathing problem - due to over-breeding, his airways are so clogged up the poor dog struggles for every breath. This leaves the vets at Battersea with no option but to take him into surgery for a major operation.

programme.sub-title: Paul O'grady For The Love Of Dogs Series 4 Ep 5
programme.desc: In this episode, Paul meets Bert, a big, bouncy Great Dane puppy. He immediately falls in love with this gentle giant but fears grow when Paul discovers that Bert is suffering from some severe growing pains. His front legs have developed 'elbow dysplasia' and are growing abnormally - surgery is the only possible remedy for Bert but there doubts how successful, if at all, any operation may be.

programme.title: Great Irish Interiors
programme.desc: Originally a hunting lodge, Fota House became a permanent residence in the 1820s and today is a centrepiece of Fota Island in County Cork. Martina Madden is the Museum Standards and Property Coordinator, and she is welcoming the grandchild of the last resident of the house back to share his memories, and surprise her with some of his own materials. As they relive his youth, plenty of work needs to be carried out on the building itself.

programme.title: Great Irish Interiors
programme.desc: Castle Ward perches on the southern shores of Strangford Lough in County Down. Built in the 1760s by Bernard Ward and his wife Lady Anne Ward, the house is famous for its dual architecture and one of Ireland's biggest ornamental canals. The entrance side of the house is done in a classical Palladian style, while the opposite side is of the Georgian gothic style, and this precedent is apparent throughout the house.

From the marriage that deemed so wrong it caused George III to write a new law to the first 'People's Princess'. Helping Suzannah unpack these stories are Dr Nicola Clark, Dr Katie Carpenter, Dr Alexandra Loske and journalist Stephen Bates.

programme.desc: Born with one finger on her left hand, Agatha was abandoned to Vivaldi's famous Venetian orphanage in 1712, where disabled girls defied convention to join an elite all female orchestra. Centuries on, ACC manager Elizabeth Anderson unearthed Agatha's near complete cantata in a Venice library. Now restored, it receives its European premiere in the splendour of the Pisani Palace.

programme.desc: What do extreme sports, doomscrolling, addiction, Parkinson's disease, and ADHD all have in common? Dopamine. This crucial neurotransmitter helps facilitate pleasure, reward, motivation, memory and movement within the body, but is that always a good thing? Insight explores when the activation of dopamine can lead to pleasure, or pain.

programme.desc: Bologna is the capital of Emilia-Romagna, home to the highest number of protected food products in the whole of Italy, known as DOP's. These products are globally renowned, strictly regulated and of exceptional quality - parmigiano, prosciutto de Parma and traditional balsamic vinegar to name but a few. One of the world's best chefs, Massimo Bottura, drives Stanley to a premium parmigiano producer, who uses the milk of the white Modenese cows.

As they relive his youth, plenty of work needs to be carried out on the building itself.

programme.title: Great Irish Interiors
programme.desc: Castle Ward perches on the southern shores of Strangford Lough in County Down. Built in the 1760s by Bernard Ward and his wife Lady Anne Ward, the house is famous for its dual architecture and one of Ireland's biggest ornamental canals. The entrance side of the house is done in a classical Palladian style, while the opposite side is of the Georgian gothic style, and this precedent is apparent throughout the house.

programme.title: Great Irish Interiors

programme.title: Great Irish Interiors
programme.desc: Castle Ward perches on the southern shores of Strangford Lough in County Down. Built in the 1760s by Bernard Ward and his wife Lady Anne Ward, the house is famous for its dual architecture and one of Ireland's biggest ornamental canals. The entrance side of the house is done in a classical Palladian style, while the opposite side is of the Georgian gothic style, and this precedent is apparent throughout the house.
